findings.title: getForLogin can return identity providers that are not available for login
findings.body: The new getForLogin cache stores only internal IDs and, on both cache miss and cache hit, reconstructs the result by calling session.identityProviders().getById(id) and adding every non-null model to the returned stream without applying IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate(). The delegate search can include organization-linked IDPs whose organization is disabled, because it filters on BROKER_PUBLIC and ORGANIZATION_ID but does not evaluate the organization's enabled state. createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel then intentionally makes isEnabled() false for such IDPs. As a result, getForLogin violates its contract by returning IDPs that are not available for login. The OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean had to add extra isEnabled() filters, but other callers will still receive disabled brokers. Filter the final stream with getLoginPredicate() or otherwise invalidate/refresh the login cache when organization enabled state changes.

findings.title: Test cleanup registers the literal alias "alias" instead of the created provider alias
findings.body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, the cleanup for each newly created identity provider is registered as testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove, using the literal string "alias" rather than the variable alias such as "idp-alias-" + i or "idp-alias-20". The same mistake is repeated at line 425. Therefore the actual created providers are not removed after the test, and cleanup may attempt to delete a nonexistent/wrong provider. Use the actual alias variable or the created provider resource in addCleanup.
